subject: Proposal: consolidate feature teams into a single product enablement group
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: consolidate feature teams into a single product enablement group

Team —

I floated a high-level idea with a few folks this morning and wanted to capture it for discussion: consolidate the two small "Feature Platform" pods (Model Serving + Integrations) into a single Product Enablement org that reports to one lead. The motivation is threefold: reduce cross-pod handoffs, create a single roadmap owner for developer experience, and establish clearer escalation paths for customer-impacting incidents.

High-level changes in the attached draft org chart and role diffs:
- Merge 6 ICs across the two pods into a single org (no net headcount change).
- Create two senior IC leads (technical owners) and one manager who focuses on deliverables and stakeholder alignment.
- Redefine role scopes so PMs and eng leads don't have overlapping responsibilities for platform stability vs. feature shipping.

Asks: please review the attached org-chart-proposal.png and role-scope-diffs.xlsx and comment on risk and gaps. I know span-of-control and career ladders are immediate concerns — flagged for Lauren and Stephanie. Marcus, can you validate the throughput and on-call impact if we consolidate? Aisha, I want your read on any customer-facing risk.

Timing: I propose a 6–8 week transition window with a town hall + 1:1s. If we like the direction, we'll align with People Ops on messaging and formal role updates.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Engineering — Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org-chart-proposal.png, role-scope-diffs.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate feature teams into a single product enablement group

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear write-up and attachments. I support the goal of fewer handoffs, but a couple of immediate concerns:
- Span of control: one manager covering ~8 ICs + two senior IC leads could be tight given our current cadence. We should model manager load for the next 12 months.
- Career ladders: we need explicit IC career progression paths (especially for platform engineers) before merging — otherwise promotion discussions get messy.
- Performance reviews: merging mid-cycle will complicate current review calibrations for two of the engineers. We should coordinate with People Ops on how to handle mid-review org moves.

Can we include a variant where we pilot a single product enablement lead for 8–10 weeks, then re-evaluate? That mitigates risk and gives us empirical data. Happy to help draft the manager load model.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Developer Experience

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate feature teams into a single product enablement group

Marissa / Lauren —

I reviewed the role diffs. A few data points from infra/serving side:
- On-call impact: combining the teams would centralize runbook ownership which is + for consistency, but we'd need two designated incident leads for coverage.
- Throughput: with current backlogs I estimate a 10–15% slowdown in feature delivery for 6–8 weeks during the transition (knowledge transfer + pairing).
- Headcount: confirm there is no net reduction — I want this explicit in the comms. We should also list who becomes the temporary tech lead for each priority area.

If we pilot (Lauren's suggestion), my preference is to keep existing sprint boundaries for the first two sprints and only change triage/ownership after that.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager — Serving Runtime

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.inference>

Marissa —

Customer impact note: a few enterprise accounts (including AcmeAI) have contracts that reference support SLAs and named technical contacts. If we change who owns which components, we need to proactively notify impacted accounts and offer a transition plan. For AcmeAI specifically, Elena Park will need a 1:1 with the new lead; Tom Sanders from procurement may ask for an updated SOW.

Also: sales-facing roadmaps need to be stable for at least 30 days during any org change. Happy to coordinate comms and outreach.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman

Thanks for the quick turns. Summary of agreed next steps:
1) Pilot model for 8 weeks starting Sept 7. No net headcount change; explicit callout in comms.
2) Marcus and Marissa to identify two incident leads and temporary tech owners by Aug 25 (deliverable: short roster).
3) Stephanie / People Ops to prepare town hall slides and a manager 1:1 script; target internal announce on Sept 1.
4) Aisha to lead customer outreach for the 5 named enterprise accounts and schedule 1:1s with Elena Park (AcmeAI) week of Sept 8.
5) Lauren to produce a manager-load model and a promotion buffer plan for any candidates mid-cycle by Aug 28.

I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call for Monday Aug 24 to lock the roster and comms. If People Ops flags anything, we'll pause.

Rohan Mehta
Head of Product Operations
